measurements.quote: grows to a height of 2–3 feet (0.61–0.91 m)
it can be as high as 8–10 ft (2.4–3.0 m)
Each clump's diameter can increase up to 4 ft (1.2 m)
leaf-blade is around 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) long

appearance.value: stems and leaves purplish and glabrous
appearance.quote: The stems and leaves have a purplish color and are glabrous

appearance.value: spikes of female and male spikelets; single raceme or panicle of two to three unisexual racemes
appearance.quote: consist of spikes made up of female and male spikelets

architecture.value: short internodes, so all leaves grow out from the plant's base
architecture.quote: all the leaves grow out from the plant's base

architecture.value: several short, fibrous, thick rhizomes; deep hollow roots from lower nodes

phenology.quote: blooms from late March to early October
The seed-producing season of the grass is from June to September

propagation.fact: seedhead joints break into two as the fruit matures, each part holding one seed
propagation.quote: The joints of the seedhead break into two as the fruit matures

uses_real.quote: widely cultivated for its use as forage

description.value: Warm-season, sod-forming bunch grass usually 0.6-0.9 m but up to 3 m, with long broad purplish leaves and spike-like flower heads.
description.quote: Usually, gamagrass grows to a height of 2–3 feet (0.61–0.91 m)

native_range.value: Eastern United States to northern South America
native_range.quote: native from the eastern United States to northern South America

environment.value: Sunny moist areas such as watercourses and wet prairies.
environment.quote: Its natural habitat is in sunny moist areas, such as along watercourses and in wet prairies

flowers.quote: The flowers of eastern gamagrass, which blooms from late March to early October

fruit.type: seed in a seedhead that breaks into joints
fruit.quote: The joints of the seedhead break into two as the fruit matures
